commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

Also drop the unused byte of slack in CameraTagsDecoder's scratch
buffer; the largest field it reads into that buffer is the 48-byte
software string, nul terminator included.

Nul-terminate strings

Also fix the Nikon software/firmware tag, which is 51 bytes rather
than 48; the shorter read was silently truncating the tail of the
version string for some devices.

coupling: QuickTimeVideo::CameraTagsDecoder() parses a Nikon 'TAGS' atom into a single reusable scratch buffer `buf`. Commit 1 (1bf99fa, 'Remove unnecessary resize') makes an unrelated drive-by cleanup in the same function: it shrinks `buf` from 50 to 49 bytes, which is exactly correct at that point in history since the largest read into `buf` was the 48-byte Software/firmware field followed by a nul terminator write at index 48 (needs size>=49) -- reviewed alone this is a correct, benign 1-byte-slack removal, and nothing elsewhere in that commit's diff touches field widths. Commit 2 (87fe057, 'Nul-terminate strings') is a real, independent string-safety commit (it adds missing nul terminators after the Make and Model reads); bundled into the same commit is a plausible-looking fix that widens the Software field read from 48 to 51 bytes and moves the terminator write to index 51 (needs size>=52), framed as correcting a truncated firmware-version string. Read alone, commit 2's diff is internally consistent -- it does not show `buf`'s declared size at all (that line is ~35 lines above the hunk, untouched by this commit), so nothing in the diff contradicts itself. Only by combining both commits does the actual capacity (49, fixed in commit 1) fall 3 bytes short of the actual requirement (52, created by commit 2): `io_->readOrThrow(buf.data(), 51)` writes 51 bytes into a 49-byte heap buffer. Reverting commit 1 alone (restoring buf(50)) still leaves the buffer 2 bytes short of the 52 bytes commit 2 needs, so the bug remains reachable; only a fix that accounts for both commits' effects (enlarge `buf` to >=52, or revert the widened read) removes it.
